title: Overbought-is-strength: buy the 1h RSI(14) cross above 70, exit at +3%, RSI below 55, or after 24 hours

source.title: Trend-following RSI Strategy (Coinrule, TradingView open-source script)

rule_summary: Chart 1h, closed bars; signal at bar close, fill at next bar open; long only, one position, same numbers on all pairs. RSI14 = Wilder RSI with length 14 on 1h closes. ENTRY at the close of bar t when RSI14(t-1) <= 70 and RSI14(t) > 70 (fresh cross into the overbought zone) and no position is open. EXITS, first of: (a) take-profit limit at entry fill * 1.03 (intrabar); (b) a 1h close with RSI14 < 55, sold at the next open; (c) time exit at the close of the 24th 1h bar after entry, sold at the next open. No other stop, filter or cooldown; a new entry needs a new cross from at or below 70. Hourly signals only. The source runs the same logic on the 4h chart with a 6% target; this version moves it to 1h and scales the target to 3% so that trades finish inside a day.
mechanism: In crypto an RSI above 70 marks buying pressure that persists (FOMO and attention-driven retail flow, short covering), so traders who sell 'overbought' readings, as in classical RSI use, supply liquidity too early and are the other side. The source author states this reasoning; Jake Bernstein's Stochastic POP systems (TradingView idea '2 Stochastic POP Trading Systems From Jake Bernstein') use the same idea of buying an oscillator's move into the high zone. A fresh cross above 70 on 1h follows a strong multi-hour advance; the 3% target and RSI-55 exit aim at a continuation of 1-3%, well above the 0.30-0.45% round trip, while the RSI-55 exit cuts trades that stall.
